title: 3D-printed booster delivers 715,000 pounds of thrust at 30% less mass
text: 3D-printed booster delivers 715,000 pounds of thrust at 30% less mass Blue Origin's Northstar engine delivers 715,000 pounds of thrust, weighs 30% less than BE-4, and uses additive manufacturing. Blue Origin unveiled Northstar, a new LOX\/LNG booster engine producing 715,000 pounds-force of thrust. The engine reached development testing just 11 months after program approval. Blue Origin has developed a new rocket engine that delivers more thrust with significantly less hardware. Called Northstar, the liquid oxygen and liquefied natural gas-fueled booster engine produces 715,000 pounds-force of thrust. It also weighs 30% less than the company’s BE-4 engine, despite delivering greater power. The new engine marks Blue Origin’s second booster propulsion system.Its development also demonstrates how advanced manufacturing techniques can simplify rocket engine production. More than 65% of Northstar’s components use additive manufacturing, reducing the number of individual parts and assembly time. Northstar could strengthen Blue Origin’s propulsion portfolio as the company expands its launch capabilities. The announcement also included a major upgrade to its New Glenn rocket, which gains a new third stage for demanding orbital missions.Northstar produces 715,000 pounds-force of thrust, compared with 640,000 pounds-force from the BE-4. That represents a substantial increase in output without adding unnecessary mass. Blue Origin says the new engine cuts overall mass by 30%. The engine also contains 50% fewer parts than its predecessor.Additive manufacturing accounts for more than 65% of its production. This approach allows engineers to consolidate components that traditionally require separate manufacturing and assembly processes. Production speed represents another significant improvement. Blue Origin says technicians can assemble Northstar in less than a day.The company has not disclosed its complete manufacturing process or the engine’s intended launch vehicle. ​World’s first laser-generated plasma antenna could enable space communications Northstar retains several established elements of Blue Origin’s propulsion architecture. It burns liquefied natural gas and liquid oxygen through an oxygen-rich staged combustion cycle. A single-shaft turbopump handles propellant delivery.That combination connects the new engine with the company’s existing propulsion technology. However, its reduced component count and manufacturing requirements offer a different approach to producing large booster engines. Northstar reached development testing just 11 months after receiving program approval. That timeline reflects a development process built around rapid design iterations and in-house manufacturing capabilities.in Blue Origin’s booster propulsion lineup.The company also develops engines for upper-stage and in-space applications, giving it several propulsion options across different mission profiles. Blue Origin also introduced GS3, a new third stage for its New Glenn rocket. The addition expands the vehicle’s ability to reach demanding orbital destinations without relying on additional spacecraft propulsion. GS3 supports direct insertion into geostationary orbit and trans-lunar injection .Its performance varies with New Glenn’s configuration. The 9×4 vehicle can carry up to 14 metric tons to GEO and 20 metric tons to TLI. The 7×2 configuration supports up to 8 metric tons to GEO and 10 metric tons to TLI. These capabilities could serve commercial satellite operators and government customers.GS3 already has a contracted cislunar mission scheduled for 2028. The stage uses Blue Origin’s BE-7 engine, which delivers more than 460 seconds of vacuum-specific impulse on GS3 mission profiles. It also supports multiple burns and extended coast periods for complex orbital maneuvers.has completed an important structural test for the stage. Engineers pressurized its composite liquid hydrogen tank to 100% of maximum expected operating pressure for 2.5 hours.They subsequently reached 150% of that pressure for 10 minutes.
